scope: Only the Yjs seam changes production behavior: a bounded eligibility probe selects a complete encoding comparison that retains long writeString values at exact byte offsets. Matching all bytes, offsets and string values proves original encoding equality; any difference reconstructs the original bytes and uses the existing exact-byte/GC-normalized fallback. State vectors, deletions and exact pending bookkeeping still run on every transition. Document/history forks, admission ordering, persistence and wire formats are unchanged. The final full unit suite passes 96 files / 1,030 tests; 150 existing and 200 new generated comparison histories agree with the frozen always-normalizing reference, and 500 fork histories remain. Ignoring retained strings fails two tests. Native pending and original-order delivery each pass 100 generated histories and their directed crash/pressure cases. Native content/publication mutants are detected. The owned workspace-admission catalogue passes ten cases and four mutations with a drained process group. The initial native pending invocation placed its output outside the unchanged Vite allow-list; that harness error and the corrected-location pass are both retained. A test-generator setup error (undefined inserted directly into Y.Array) is retained and corrected without product changes. All exploratory, intermediate and final performance samples and final bundle identities survive. The final alternating comparison-only medians (baseline/candidate) are 1.555/0.280 ms at 1k items, 3.295/3.296 at 10k and 17.791/17.825 at 100k, with 100k visible characters. Sequential full-command results remain mixed. These are dependent single-host observations, not population or causal estimates. The bounded construction and decision conditions were specified in docs/f17-comparison.md.
